sources.entry: AppBox - Tool for iOS developers to build and deploy Development, Ad-Hoc and In-house (Enterprise) applications directly to the devices from your Dropbox account.

summary.one_liner: AppBox is a macOS tool that lets iOS developers deploy Development, Ad-Hoc and In-house (Enterprise) app builds wirelessly to devices using links hosted through a connected Dropbox account.
summary.what_it_does: AppBox uploads an IPA file and makes it installable on devices through a shareable link, using the user's Dropbox account for hosting. The README lists features such as keeping the same install link for an app across versions, installing previous versions via that link, and auto-emailing the distribution link. Uploads automatically restart after a network change or failure. It has a setup assistant, a dashboard for managing uploaded apps, and webhook integration with Slack, Microsoft Teams and Hangout Chat. It also mentions Fastlane support, with details behind a "read more" link not included in the README. A standalone command-line tool (appboxcli) is distributed alongside the app.
use_cases: distribute iOS test builds to testers wirelessly
share ad-hoc iOS app builds with clients
deploy in-house enterprise iOS apps to devices
install iOS apps over the air from a link
send app install links by email automatically
notify team chat channels about new app builds
how_to_run: curl -s | bash (install script; URL not included in the README)
Download AppBox.dmg from Releases and drag AppBox.app into Applications
Link your Dropbox account in AppBox, then select or drag an IPA file and click upload
notable: Keeps the same installation link for an app across versions, and can install previous versions via that link
No app size limit and no expiration for uploaded apps, per the README feature list
Auto-restarts uploads after network changes or failures
Standalone appboxcli command-line tool released alongside the GUI app
Webhook integration for Slack, Microsoft Teams and Hangout Chat
caveats: Depends on a linked Dropbox account for hosting the uploaded apps
License terms shown are a Creative Commons-style text (Attribution, NoDerivatives) that the README does not name explicitly
